title: Eagle view: a new terminal takes the whole empty space it lands in, not half the height
summary: In eagle view a new terminal or pre-launch card landing in an empty space of a custom layout was capped at the automatic grid's tile size, so after Tidy up it filled only half of a free full-height column. The cap is gone: a new tile takes the whole largest empty rectangle; 2 tests added, 1 updated, runbook and changelog updated.
lessons_learned: CI's Frontend job (pr-checks.yml) runs typecheck, lint and tests but no `npm run build`, so a merge on green CI does not prove the Vite build; the reviewer ran the build by hand this run. Either add the build step to CI or keep running it in review.

deferred.what: With the size cap gone, the first new tile takes the whole empty space, so a second new tile added to the same layout splits a terminal the user placed instead of sharing that space (two cards added after closing one of three tidied terminals: card 1 gets the free column, card 2 halves a stored terminal, and the next move or resize stores the halved place).
deferred.why: The issue fixed 'uncapped' and left the split branch unchanged; sharing a hole between several new tiles, or splitting a new tile before a stored one, is a design choice.
